In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rifampin is an extremely potent antituberculous agent, and that it should be given in doses that can be tolerated to achieve a free Cmax-to-MIC ratio of >175.

the pharmacokinetic-pharmocodynamic parameters that determine the effect of rifamycin derivatives are (i) the area under the free concentration-time curve-to-inhibitory quotient, (ii) free peak concentration-to-MIC ratio, and (iii ) the duration that the free concentration is above MIC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the killing and prevention of resistance of rifampin are linked to the area-under-the-concentration-time-curve-to-MIC ratio and that the duration of the postantibiotic-effect is linked to the free Cmax-to-MIC ratio.
rifampin is a highly effective drug for the treatment of tuberculosis, but that its concentration dependence may limit its use for intermittent therapy.
the concentration of the drug in the target organism is a key factor for the activity of rifampin and that the free Cmax/MC ratio is the most important parameter for the suppression of resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current dose and dosing regimen of rifampin may not be optimal for tuberculosis treatment.
the pharmacokinetics of rifampin are not the major limiting factors for its use in intermittent therapy.
rifampin's activity is not limited by its short half-life, and that the development of new rifamycin congeners should not focus on prolonging rifampin's elimination half-life.
